name: EP-14 Revenue Engine (Backlog)
w: Turn the hostel manager into a platform that earns three ways: subscriptions from owners, a small fee on the rent and deposits that flow through it, and commissions on services sold to owners and residents. Ordered by expected revenue per unit of effort; the first four can carry the business on their own.
ac: Hostels pay for their plan inside the app
Rent is collected online, with a per-transaction margin
At least one partner service (verification, financing, insurance) earns a commission
Owners and residents have reasons to stay (resident app, automation) that keep churn low
out: No lending or insurance on our own balance sheet: always through licensed partners.
dod: Ideas only. Each task is detailed and estimated again when scheduled.

name: Charge hostels for their plan
w: Recurring revenue. Today plans and trials are tracked in /admin but nothing charges for them. Price per bed in use (for example ₹15-25 per bed per month, with a minimum), so revenue grows with each hostel.
ac: Pricing tiers per bed with a monthly minimum, configurable in /admin
Owner pays by UPI AutoPay or card through the gateway's subscriptions; GST invoice emailed each month
Failed payment: reminders over 7 days, then the hostel is suspended with the existing suspension flow
Trial converts to paid without re-entering anything
out: Needs a payment gateway account (Razorpay or similar) with subscriptions enabled, and GST registration.

name: Online rent collection with UPI AutoPay
w: The biggest lever. Residents pay rent by UPI link or recurring mandate; each payment is recorded automatically. Earns a margin per transaction (or a convenience fee the owner chooses to pass on) and makes the product very hard to leave, because collection stops working without it.
ac: Pay link per invoice, sent with the existing WhatsApp reminder
Optional monthly UPI AutoPay mandate per resident
Gateway webhook records the payment against the invoice, verified and idempotent
Settlement report per hostel; failed and refunded payments handled
Owner sees what share of rent was collected online
out: Needs a gateway account with route/split settlements and KYC for each owner.

name: Automatic late fees
w: Owners lose money and time chasing late rent. Rules that add a late fee on their own make collection self-enforcing, and are a strong reason to pay for a higher plan.
ac: Owner sets a rule: flat amount or percentage, after N days, optional cap
Fee added as a separate invoice line on the first overdue day, never twice
Owner can waive a late fee with a reason, logged
Residents see the fee and the rule in their reminder

name: Paid automated reminders add-on
w: A monthly add-on per hostel. Reminders and receipts go out on WhatsApp on a schedule, without anyone pressing send.
ac: Schedule: before due, on due date, every N days overdue
Uses approved WhatsApp Business templates through a provider, behind the existing NotificationChannel
Delivery status recorded in reminder_log; failures retried and shown
Priced per hostel per month, turned on in /admin
out: Needs a WhatsApp Business API provider account and approved templates.

name: Resident app (installable web app)
w: Residents seeing their dues and paying in two taps lifts online collection, and gives every resident a reason to tell the owner to stay on the platform. Also the channel for selling the partner services below.
ac: Sign in with mobile OTP
See dues, pay, download receipts, see deposit held
Raise a complaint (plumbing, electricity, cleaning) and follow its status
Read hostel notices
Installable on the phone home screen
out: No native iOS or Android app at first.

name: Public vacancy pages and lead marketplace
w: A new revenue line that also fills beds. Each hostel can publish a page with photos, prices and live vacant beds (already known from occupancy). Students searching 'PG near <college>' find it and send an enquiry. Charge for featured placement or per qualified lead.
ac: Public page per hostel, opt-in, with live vacancy by sharing type
Search by city, area and price; fast and indexable
Enquiry form sends the lead to the owner (and WhatsApp); leads tracked
Featured listing and pay-per-lead billing through E14-T1
out: No booking or payment for a bed through the marketplace at first.

name: Tenant verification as a paid service
w: Owners must verify residents (police verification is required in many cities) and today do it on paper. Charge per check, with a margin over the verification provider's price.
ac: Aadhaar/DigiLocker based identity check from the resident profile, with the resident's consent
Police verification form pre-filled for the hostel's city
Result and date stored on the resident; never the full ID number
Charged per check on the hostel's monthly bill
out: Needs a licensed KYC/verification provider; follows DPDP consent rules already in place.

name: Deposit and rent financing through a partner
w: Deposits of two to three months' rent stop many students moving in. 'Pay your deposit in 3 parts' through an NBFC partner fills beds faster; the partner pays a referral fee per loan, and the owner still receives the full deposit.
ac: Offer shown at allocation and in the resident app
Partner's own flow for credit checks and agreements
Owner receives the full deposit; the deposit ledger records it as collected
Referral fees reported in /admin
out: We never lend or hold credit risk: only a licensed NBFC partner does.

name: Resident insurance and services marketplace
w: Commission on services residents already buy: belongings insurance, laundry, tiffin and food, mattress rental. Small per sale, but across thousands of residents every month.
ac: Partner catalogue per city, shown in the resident app
Purchases through the partner, tracked by referral code
Commission reports per partner and per hostel
Owner can turn the marketplace off for their hostel
out: Needs partner agreements; insurance only through a licensed insurer or broker.

name: Mess and electricity billing
w: Many PGs charge for meals and electricity separately and work it out in a notebook. Adding them to the monthly invoice saves hours and is a premium-plan feature.
ac: Meal plans per resident (veg/non-veg, meals per day) priced monthly and pro-rated
Electricity per room from meter readings, split across residents by nights
Both appear as invoice lines in the monthly run
Readings and plans have history; nothing is edited after billing
out: No smart-meter integration at first; readings are entered by staff.

name: Chain plan for multi-property owners
w: Operators with 5 to 50 properties pay the most and churn the least. A chain plan is the top price tier.
ac: Consolidated dashboard: occupancy, collections and dues across all properties
Reports comparable across properties and exportable
Staff who work across several properties with per-property roles
Bulk actions: rates and invoice runs for several properties at once
out: No accounting-system integration in this task.

name: Owner referral programme
w: PG owners know each other; word of mouth is the cheapest growth channel. A free month for each referred hostel that starts paying.
ac: Referral code per owner, shareable on WhatsApp
Credit applied automatically when the referred hostel pays its first month
Referrals and credits visible to the owner and in /admin

name: Churn and upsell signals in /admin
w: Keeping a customer is cheaper than finding one. Show the operator which hostels are slipping and which are ready for a bigger plan.
ac: Flag hostels with falling activity (no payments or allocations recorded for 14 days)
List trials ending in the next 14 days with their usage
Flag hostels near their plan's bed limit or with several properties (chain plan candidates)
Weekly summary for the operator
out: No automated outreach in this task.
